Why this, and why now.

01

Compact code models can run on one consumer GPU.

Which of them is good enough for real project work is exactly what this proposal says must be qualified through trials, not assumed.

02

People re-explain their project every session.

Decisions, conventions and constraints live in heads and old threads. Memory with a source turns them into something you can inspect and correct.

03

Teams ask where their code goes.

Keeping project data on the machine by default removes a whole class of questions. Anything remote would be opt-in, per project.

Starting narrow on purpose: Windows 11, VS Code, React with TypeScript. Each layer expands only once it can be checked.

Good questions.

Take the product brief↓
What exactly is Blue Nebula?

The working name for a proposed local-first AI engineering workspace. It connects a repository, visual canvas, persistent project memory, local models and visible verification. It is an application layer, not an operating system kernel.

Can I download the desktop app today?

No. This site presents the product vision and an interactive browser concept. The downloadable brief explains the proposed scope, hardware assumptions and roadmap.

Does this demo call an AI model?

No. The demo uses editable example data and deterministic stages. Everything runs in your browser. It does not index a repository, execute generated code or connect to a local model.

Will my projects need a cloud connection?

The proposal is local storage and inference by default, with an offline supported workflow after installation. Optional remote providers would require explicit permission. These are requirements awaiting implementation.

Which tools and machines are in scope?

The proposed starting point is Windows 11 x64, VS Code and React with TypeScript. A 32 GB RAM system with 12 GB NVIDIA VRAM is the reference inference profile; a 16 GB CPU profile is best effort.

How is memory different from training?

Project memory keeps inspectable facts outside model weights, where they can be corrected or deleted. Optional adapter training is a later, separately consented capability. Saving a memory does not train a model.
